qt: to the Commission Ville Niinistö (Verts/ALE), Maria Ohisalo (Verts/ALE) Subject:

The American mink is listed as an invasive alien species. Finland is nevertheless seeking a derogation to continue mink fur farming, which requires compelling reasons of public interest. These are hard to identify, since the sector is not economically feasible and fur farming carries serious animal welfare and zoonotic risks. Finland is allocating almost EUR 100 million in subsidies to the fur farming sector and it is now one of the few Member States still holding on to an industry that most others have banned or are phasing out. The Commission’s response to the ‘Fur Free Europe’ European citizens’ initiative, signed by more than 1.5 million citizens, was due by March 2026. It has still not been delivered. 1.

What criteria will the Commission apply when assessing any Finnish derogation request, and will it take account of animal welfare, pandemic risk and the sector’s minimal economic weight and non-existent competitiveness, so that the scientifically based listing is not undermined?
Why has the Commission not yet replied to the citizens’ initiative, when will it do so, and will it propose an EU-wide ban on fur farming?
Will the Commission refrain from accepting any derogation for mink fur farming until it has responded to the initiative?
